newsitem.title: CHINA: China dissident Chen Ziming released for treatment.
newsitem.headline: China dissident Chen Ziming released for treatment.

text.p: China released leading dissident Chen Ziming from prison on Wednesday to allow him to receive medical treatment, a family member said.
Chen's release came a week after a Beijing court jailed former student leader Wang Dan for 11 years after a brief trial that prompted expressions of concern from around the world.
"His wife went to meet him... He's at his own home," Chen's mother Wu Yongfen said by telephone.
"Because he is ill, he asked to be released on bail for medical treatment," Wu said, adding it was unclear how long Chen would be permitted to remain at liberty.

Chen, 42, was sentenced to a 13-year prison term in 1991 for engaging in "counter-revolutionary", or subversive, activities during the ill-fated 1989 pro-democracy protests centred on Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
He won medical parole in 1994 in a move widely seen as a successful bid by Beijing to prevent Washington from revoking China's Most Favoured Nation trade status on grounds of human rights violations.
Human rights have been a persistent irritant in Sino-U.S. ties already strained by disputes over trade, copyright piracy, arms proliferation and Taiwan.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher is scheduled to arrive in Beijing this month for a visit widely seen as a vital step to rebuilding the cross-Pacific relationship.
It was unclear whether Chen, who has been treated for cancer and hepatitis and suffers from a number of other ailments, would be imprisoned again after treatment, his mother said.
"Last time, in 1994, he was also released on bail for medical treatment and later they made him go back," she said.
Chen was returned to prison on June 25, 1995, after joining calls for Beijing to release political prisoners and reverse its verdict that the Tiananmen Square protests were seditious.

His latest release by Chinese authorities came amid continuing condemnation from international human rights groups over the jailing of Wang Dan last Wednesday after a trial lasting less than four hours.
The United States and other nations expressed deep concern over the verdict and sentence.
Wang, a dissident also known for his role as a leader of the 1989 Tiananmen protests, had pleaded not guilty to subversion charges carrying a maximum death sentence.

His 11-year sentence was the latest in a series of crushing blows against China's embattled band of dissidents, most of whom are already either in exile or serving long terms in jail or administrative detention.
